stages.title: Language sounds and pronunciation
explain: Italian is spelled almost as it sounds. It has five vowels: a, e, i, o, u, and each one is clear and short. Every vowel in a word is said.
Double consonants are really said long: "pala" (shovel) and "palla" (ball) are different words. The letter h is silent, and "ci" sounds like English "chee", while "chi" sounds like "kee".

o: The double l is held longer
gq.why: Double consonants are said longer and change the meaning.
In Italian, ch before i is a hard k sound.

panel.q: Why is "ciao" said with a "ch" sound but "chi" with a "k" sound?
o: Ci gives a soft sound; chi keeps it hard
Because i is silent in chi
panel.why: The h keeps c hard before e or i.

panel.q: Why is spelling easier in Italian than in English?
o: Letters usually match the same sounds
panel.why: Italian spelling is quite regular.

panel.q: A learner says "pala" for "palla". What error is this?
panel.why: Gemination is a key feature of Italian pronunciation.

points.ask: How do I say chi and ci?

teach.model: Italian is read as it is written. The five vowels are clear. Double consonants are held longer, like palla. Ci sounds like chee and chi like kee.

stages.hook: Say "casa", "pizza" and "gelato". Does Italian say the letters the way they are written?
stages.mnemonic: Italian is a song: every vowel sings, double letters hold on.

stages.title: Alphabet, script or basic characters
explain: Italian has 21 basic letters. It leaves out j, k, w, x and y, which appear only in foreign words like "jazz" or "whisky".
The letter names are: a, bi, ci, di, e, effe, gi, acca, i, elle, emme, enne, o, pi, cu, erre, esse, ti, u, vi, zeta. Accents appear on final vowels, as in "città" and "caffè".

gq.q: Which letters are not in the basic Italian alphabet?
gq.why: They appear only in loanwords such as jazz.

gq.q: Where do written accents usually appear in Italian?
o: On the last vowel of a word
gq.why: Words like città and caffè carry a stress mark on the final vowel.

panel.q: Why does "città" have an accent?
o: It marks stress on the final syllable
panel.why: Stress normally falls earlier, so final stress is written.

panel.q: How do you spell your name in Italian on the phone?
o: Using the Italian letter names or city names
panel.why: Italians often use city names like Roma, Milano, Napoli for letters.

panel.q: Why is the missing "k" no problem for a word like "kiwi"?
panel.why: Foreign words such as kiwi keep their original spelling.

teach.model: Italian has 21 letters. J, k, w, x and y only appear in foreign words. Accents mark stress on a final vowel, like città.

stages.hook: The Italian alphabet has fewer letters than English. Which letters are missing?
stages.mnemonic: Twenty-one letters, no J, K, W, X, Y.

stages.title: Greetings and introductions
explain: Say "ciao" to friends and family, and "buongiorno" to be polite. In the evening say "buonasera". To say goodbye, say "arrivederci".
To say your name, say "Mi chiamo" and your name. To ask, say "Come ti chiami?" with a friend. With someone formal, say "Come si chiama?".

gq.q: Which greeting is polite for an older person you do not know?
Someone says "Grazie". What do you answer?
gq.why: Prego is the usual reply to thanks.

panel.q: What is the difference between "Come stai?" and "Come sta?"
o: Stai is informal, sta is formal
panel.why: Italian uses tu for friends and Lei for polite address.

panel.q: Why does Italian say "Mi chiamo" and not "Io sono chiamo"?
o: Chiamarsi is a reflexive verb meaning "to be called"
It's a short form of essere
Italian has no verb to be
panel.why: Mi chiamo literally means "I call myself".

panel.q: Why can "ciao" be used both for hello and goodbye?
o: It is an informal greeting for meeting and parting
panel.why: Ciao works in both directions among friends.

points.ask: How do I say my name?

teach.model: Say ciao to friends and buongiorno to be polite. Say buonasera in the evening. Say arrivederci to leave. To give your name say Mi chiamo.

stages.hook: How do you greet a friend and an older neighbour in Italian? Are they the same?
stages.mnemonic: Ciao is both hi and bye; buongiorno is "good day".

stages.title: Numbers and counting
explain: Count: uno, due, tre, quattro, cinque, sei, sette, otto, nove, dieci. Then undici (11), dodici (12), tredici (13), venti (20), trenta (30).
Numbers in Italian are easy to build. For 21 say "ventuno", for 22 say "ventidue". To say your age, use avere: "Ho dieci anni" literally means "I have ten years".

gq.q: How do you say "I am ten years old"?

panel.q: Why is it "ventuno" and not "venti uno"?
o: Compound numbers are written as one word
panel.why: Venti loses its final i before uno and otto, and the number is written as one word.

panel.q: How is 28 written?
panel.why: Venti loses its final i before otto and uno.

panel.q: Why is "sei" easy to mix up with "sei" (you are)?
o: They are spelled the same but differ by context
panel.why: Sei means both six and you are; context decides.

points.ask: How do I count to three?
How do I give my age?

teach.model: Italian numbers go uno, due, tre up to dieci. Then undici, dodici, tredici. Twenty is venti and thirty is trenta. To say your age use avere: Ho dieci anni.

stages.hook: Can you count to ten in Italian? Which numbers are close to Spanish or French?
stages.mnemonic: Uno, due, tre: one, two, three; dieci is ten, let us see.

stages.title: Colours and shapes
explain: The Italian flag is "verde, bianco e rosso" (green, white and red). Colours come after the noun: "una macchina rossa".
Colours in -o change: rosso, rossa, rossi, rosse. Colours in -e, like verde, only change in the plural: verdi. Common shapes are il cerchio, il quadrato and il triangolo.

gq.q: What is the feminine form of "rosso"?
gq.why: Adjectives in -o change to -a for feminine singular.

gq.q: Choose the correct form: due case ___
gq.why: Case is feminine plural, so bianca becomes bianche.

panel.q: Why does "verde" not change in "una casa verde"?
o: Adjectives in -e have the same singular form for both genders
panel.why: Adjectives in -e change only for the plural.

panel.q: Why is the plural of "bianca" spelled "bianche"?
o: The h keeps the hard k sound before e
panel.why: Without the h, ce would sound like "che" in chair.

panel.q: Why can "blu" and "rosa" stay the same in the plural?
panel.why: Some loanword colours do not change.

teach.model: Italian colours usually follow the noun. Adjectives in -o change for gender and number: rosso, rossa, rossi, rosse. Adjectives in -e only change in the plural.

stages.hook: What colours do you see on the Italian flag? How do you say them?
stages.mnemonic: Verde, bianco, rosso: the flag has three colours in a row.

stages.title: Family and people
explain: Family words: la madre (mother), il padre (father), il fratello (brother), la sorella (sister). Children say "mamma" and "papà".
With singular family members Italian does not use an article before mio or mia: "mia madre", "mio padre". With plural or other words it does: "i miei genitori", "la mia casa".

gq.why: With a singular family member the article is usually dropped.
Genitori is masculine plural, so use i miei.

panel.q: Why do we say "la mia casa" but "mia madre"?
o: The article is dropped only with singular family terms
panel.why: This is a special rule for close family.

panel.q: What does "genitori" mean?
panel.why: Genitori means parents, a false friend for English speakers who may think of "genitals" or "gentlemen".

panel.q: Why does Italian use "nonno" and "nonna" for grandparents?
o: Each is one gendered word ending in -o or -a
panel.why: Italian nouns usually show gender with -o and -a.

points.ask: How do I say mum and dad?
When do I drop the article?

teach.model: Family words show gender: il padre and la madre. Use mio for masculine, mia for feminine and i miei for plural. For one close relative we drop the article: mia madre.

stages.hook: Who is in your family? How do you say "my mother" in Italian?
stages.mnemonic: Mia madre, mio padre: no article for one family member.

stages.title: Common objects
explain: Every Italian noun is masculine or feminine. Masculine nouns often end in -o, feminine ones in -a: il libro, la tavola. The articles are il, lo, la, l' and the plurals i, gli, le.
Use "un" or "una" for "a": un libro, una sedia. Plurals change the ending: il libro becomes i libri, la sedia becomes le sedie.
sentences: The book is on the table.

panel.q: Why is it "lo zaino" and not "il zaino"?
o: Lo goes before s plus consonant and z
panel.why: Lo is used before z, gn, ps and s plus consonant.

panel.q: Why is it "l'amico" but "l'amica" too?
o: L' is used before a vowel for both genders
panel.why: Both lo and la elide before a vowel.

panel.q: A learner says "il scuola". What is wrong?
o: Scuola is feminine, so it takes la
panel.why: La is the feminine article.

points.ask: How do I know the gender?
How do I make a plural?

teach.model: Italian nouns are masculine or feminine. Masculine often end in -o and feminine in -a. Use il or lo for masculine and la for feminine. Plurals end in -i or -e.

stages.hook: Look around you. Can you name five things in Italian?
stages.mnemonic: -o is masculine, -a is feminine; -i and -e make them plural.

stages.title: Everyday actions
explain: Many Italian verbs end in -are, like parlare. Drop -are and add -o for io: parlo. For tu add -i, for lui or lei add -a: parli, parla.
Two key verbs are essere (to be) and avere (to have): io sono, tu sei, lui è and io ho, tu hai, lui ha. For "we", add -iamo: parliamo.

panel.q: Why can Italians often drop "io" and say only "parlo"?
o: The verb ending shows the person
panel.why: The ending already marks who is speaking.

panel.q: Why does "mangiare" become "mangiamo" and not "mangiiamo"?
o: The i of the stem merges with -iamo
panel.why: Verbs in -iare lose one i.

panel.q: What is wrong with "io sono fame"?
o: Io must go at the end
panel.why: Hunger is expressed as "I have hunger".

teach.model: Take a verb in -are and remove the ending. Add -o for io, -i for tu and -a for lui or lei. Add -iamo for noi. For example parlo, parli, parliamo.

stages.hook: What do you do every day? Can you say "I eat, I play, I run" in Italian?
stages.mnemonic: -o, -i, -a: I, you, he go in a row.

stages.title: Simple listening and speaking
explain: Italian is syllable-timed. Each syllable gets similar time, and every vowel is said. Stress usually falls on the second-to-last syllable, as in "ragazzo" (ra-GAZ-zo).
To follow speech, listen for small key words like ciao, grazie, sì and no. Ask for help with "Può ripetere?" or "Più lentamente, per favore."

gq.q: Where does the stress usually fall in Italian?
gq.why: Most Italian words are stressed on the penultimate syllable.

gq.q: How do you politely ask someone to repeat?
gq.why: Può ripetere is polite and uses Lei.

panel.q: Why does an accent appear in "città" and "perché"?
o: It marks final stress that would not be expected
panel.why: Final stress is written with an accent.

panel.q: Why can "capisco" help in a conversation?
o: It tells the speaker how much you follow
panel.why: Saying capisco or non capisco guides the speaker.

panel.q: Why is it important to say every vowel when listening to Italian?
panel.why: Italian vowels are never swallowed.

points.ask: How do I ask to repeat?

teach.model: Italian is said syllable by syllable and every vowel is heard. Stress usually falls on the second-to-last syllable. If you do not understand, say Non capisco and ask Può ripetere?

stages.hook: Listen closely. When Italians talk fast, how do you find where a word ends?
